architect.description: Write the design doc for a feature: ask a few questions up front, then one plain-language document with diagrams, and revise it from the human's comments. Use when the user asks to design a feature or change that the engineer will build from.

doc-writer.description: Owns user-facing documentation. Use when creating or updating the project README, end-user guides, concept explanations, how-tos, or reference pages derived from internal architecture and design docs.

product-owner.description: Owns the product end-to-end — roadmap, milestones, feature requests, bug reports, and ideas. Use when the user wants to plan features, prioritise work, file issues, triage bugs, break work into milestones, track open TODOs, identify documentation gaps, assess product direction, or decide what to build next.

researcher.description: Research state-of-the-art approaches for technical problems outside the feature pipeline and produce concise design documents. Use when the user asks to research, evaluate, or recommend a technical approach.

reviewer.description: Review code and tests against the design doc and run the real tools. Identify correctness bugs, deviations from the design, security issues, weakened tests and test gaps; write the review guide and the merge-risk line. Use when code is ready for review before merging.

security-reviewer.description: Review a change that touches a risky area for security problems: run the installed scanners on the diff, trace untrusted input to risky operations, and report only findings with a concrete attack path. A second run tries to disprove each finding. Read-only. Use when the change touches auth, parsing, shell, file paths, secrets, dependencies, CI or similar, or when the reviewer asks for it.

software-engineer.description: Build production-ready code from an approved design doc, writing tests and code together in small, working increments. Use when there is a design doc or a Quick plan to implement.
